experiment: Linux client / Mac fixture: adjacent direct HTTPS and reverse-SSH pairs

network.physical_path: Same wired Ethernet for both; limited to 1 Gb/s by Mac link
network.ssh: Linux BEAM -> 127.0.0.1:8454 -> reverse SSH over 10.0.0.3:22 <-> 10.0.0.2 -> same Mac fixture 10.0.0.2:8454
network.tls: Repository test CA, verify_peer, localhost certificate name; per-BEAM resolver only

fixture_command: ERL_FLAGS='+S 4:4' BENCH_BIND_IP=10.0.0.2 BENCH_PORT=8454 mix run server.exs
client_command: ERL_FLAGS='+S 4:4' BENCH_PORT=8454 python3 mixed_comparison.py --clients typesafe,finch,req,req_llm --rates 3000,6000,8000,10000 --seconds 15 --repetitions 3 --network-pair results/network-pair/direct.inetrc results/network-pair/ssh.inetrc --output results/network-pair/paired
scheduling: Three randomized complete blocks, 16 client/rate combinations each. Each pair is adjacent; same combination reverses path order each repetition. Eight direct-first and eight SSH-first pairs in every block. With three repetitions each combination necessarily has a 2:1 first-order split.

hosts.linux: Intel i5-1135G7, 4 physical/8 logical CPUs, Linux7.1.5-76070105-generic, powersave governor unchanged
hosts.mac: Apple M4 Max, 16 physical/logical CPUs, macOS26.6.2 (25G83)

constraints: Normal background activity retained; no power/cooling/governor changes. Fresh client VM per case, four schedulers each client and fixture. No real Jev calls or credentials.
